answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that thaws slowly like a glacier, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Reputation then accrues only through verified completed work: a single sonnet of honest history outweighs a nebula of empty profiles. Attackers whose fake identities are caught lose their locked stake, making forgery cost more than any reward it could extract.
